messages:
sam: FYI, canary traffic shows a p95 jump after yesterday's model onboard. CI alerted +25% p95 for text-gen on the new checkpoint. Repro in staging too.

jin: Ugh. Do you have numbers / a profile?

sam: quick summary: baseline p95 ~220ms, canary ~275ms. End-to-end token throughput down ~15%. Attached profiler snippet in next message.

sam: ```
kernel-selection: chosen=matmul_fused_v2
seq_len=128
batch_size=1->4 oscillation observed when batching heuristic tries to up-batch then falls back
KV cache hit-rate drop: 0.94 -> 0.62 (post-onboard)
CPU spin: batch_scheduler waiting 14ms more on average
```

eva: interesting — KV hit-rate drop smells like tokenizer tokenization shift + different BPE offsets. That alone can cause cache key mismatches. Did the model change checkpoint tokenization?

liam: Tokenizer diff is small but the new vocab introduced 3 merging rules, offsets changed for ~2% of tokens. That could break prefix caching keys.

maya: Also saw a change in kernel heuristic merged yesterday (PR def456) where we choose fused kernel only if predicted batch growth > 1.6. For bursts it flips between kernels, which can cause tail latency oscillation when batch scheduler probes.

sam: So two potential contributors: tokenizer-induced KV cache churn + kernel selection oscillation/spin when batch size visits certain thresholds. Both would raise p95.

jin: Can we bisect to confirm? Start from last-green commit -> HEAD on staging. I'd focus on two ranges: tokenizer changes (commit range a1b2..a1b2+3) and heuristic change (def456).

liam: I'll run a quick bisect on staging metrics. Command I use: ```
./tools/stage-bisect --metric p95 --baseline 220 --target 275 --range a1b2..HEAD 
```
I'll also collect kernel selection logs: ```
TRACE=kernel_select,kv_cache ./bin/profiler --output /tmp/prof.json --run 5000
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment 202-2024-11-07T09:12:07Z for service inference-api was started by @sam.

maya: If it's KV key mismatch, a quick mitigation is to warm the KV cache with a token-normalization pass or pin the old tokenizer for canary. Rolling restart won't help until keys are normalized.

sam: I can open a quick revert of the tokenizer merge to test. But if kernel heuristic is the main culprit, reverting tokenizer won't fully fix p95.

eva: Can we get a unit-level repro? Small script that runs typical request distribution and prints kernel choice and cache hit/miss per request. If we can reproduce locally, bisect is faster.

liam: sharing a simple repro loop: ```
for q in samples.jsonl:
  ./bin/serve_request --text "$q" --trace kernel_select,kv_key | tee /tmp/run.log
```
Look for lines: `KV:miss key=...` and `kernel=matmul_fused_v2` toggles.

jin: I kicked off an automated job to compare kernel-selection histograms before/after. ETA ~8m.

sam: Job result: kernel hot vs fallback toggles increased by 3x on canary. Also KV miss spikes aligned with tokenizer tokenization differences. Timeline aligns with the tokenizer PR and the heuristic PR landing within the same release window.

maya: So likely interaction: tokenizer changed token boundaries -> KV cache key change -> cache miss increases -> smaller effective batchable prefixes -> batch heuristic reacts and flips kernels -> scheduler oscillation -> tail latency spikes. Cascading failure.

eva: Good root cause hypothesis. Short term mitigation options:
- revert tokenizer to restore KV key stability (fast test)
- pin kernel heuristic to previous safe threshold (stop oscillation)
- prewarm KV with normalized keys (workaround)

sam: I'll open two PRs: revert tokenizer for canary, and a toggle to force stable kernel selection (old heuristic) behind a runtime flag.

liam: I'll prepare a warmup job that replays top-10k prefixes to rebuild KV keys for canary traffic.

jin: Also add a regression test: tokenization-stable check that computes forward/backward token sequence equality for top-1000 queries in our eval corpus. Block tokenizer merges if mismatch > 0.5%.

ops-bot: alert: staging-bisect-job finished. Suspicious commits: a1b2c3 (tokenizer rules), def456 (batch heuristic).

maya: Nice. Can we sequence: revert tokenizer -> observe canary p95. If still elevated, flip kernel heuristic flag -> observe. That will isolate.

sam: Plan acknowledged. I'll revert tokenizer PR to a temporary branch and deploy to canary now. Will report numbers in ~10m.

eva: Postmortem action items so far: add tokenization stability CI, add KV-key migration docs, add kernel heuristic shadowing for 24h after heuristic changes, and add an automated warmup job for onboards.

jin: Thanks team. If anyone sees other odd logs (alloc spikes or scheduler errors) paste them here.

sam: Update: after reverting tokenizer on canary p95 returned to ~225ms, KV hit-rate back up to 0.91. Still slightly worse than baseline — keeping the kernel heuristic flag ready to flip.

liam: Good signal. I'll start the warmup replay for prod canary.

maya: I'll follow up with a small RFC to change the heuristic to be less sensitive to transient batch growth.

sam: Closing loop here — will open the revert PR and a follow-up RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
